questions.prompt: A capacitor has capacitance \(C\) and voltage \(v\) across it. Which relation is the element law?
questions.explanation: Charge is \(q = Cv\), and current is the derivative of charge, so \(i = C\,dv/dt\). The inductor law is the one that puts a derivative on the current: \(v = L\,di/dt\). Putting \(C\) in that slot mixes the two storage elements. \(i = Cv\) and \(i = v/C\) are algebraic, like a resistor, and a capacitor does not obey Ohm's law.

questions.prompt: A \(4\ \mathrm{kg}\) mass slides with viscous friction \(8\ \mathrm{N\,s/m}\) and no spring. A constant \(24\ \mathrm{N}\) force is applied. What speed does it settle to, in m/s?
questions.explanation:
Newton's law along the motion is \(4\dot v = 24 - 8v\). At rest \(\dot v = 0\), so \(v = 24/8 = 3\ \mathrm{m/s}\). The mass sets how fast the speed approaches that value. It does not set the value.
• \(24/4 = 6\) is the initial acceleration in \(\mathrm{m/s^2}\), if the mass starts from rest, not a speed.
• \(8/4 = 2\) is the reciprocal of the time constant, in \(\mathrm{s^{-1}}\).
• \(24 imes 8\) multiplies the two coefficients.

questions.prompt: A tank of surface area \(A\) is filled by a volume flow \(q_\mathrm{in}\). The outflow is linearized as \(q_\mathrm{out} = h/R\). Which height equation matches the volume balance?
questions.explanation: Volume in the tank is \(Ah\). Its derivative equals inflow minus outflow, so \(A\dot h = q_\mathrm{in} - h/R\). Putting \(A\) on the wrong side makes the time constant \(1/(AR)\) instead of \(AR\). A plus sign on the outflow says the tank is filling from the drain, which is unstable and physically backwards. Dropping \(A\) is right only for a tank of unit area.

questions.prompt: A coil \(L = 0.5\ \mathrm{H}\) is in series with \(R = 4\ \Omega\), and \(12\ \mathrm{V}\) is applied. The current starts at \(0\). What current does it settle to, in A?
questions.explanation:
The loop law is \(0.5\,\dot\imath + 4\imath = 12\). In steady state \(\dot\imath = 0\), so \(\imath = 12/4 = 3\ \mathrm{A}\). The inductance sets the time constant \(L/R = 0.125\ \mathrm{s}\). It stores energy. It does not drop DC voltage.
• \(12/0.5 = 24\) divides by the inductance and gives the initial \(\mathrm{d}\imath/\mathrm{d}t\) in amperes per second.
• \(0.5/4 = 0.125\) is the time constant in seconds.
• \(12 imes 4 = 48\) multiplies the source by the resistance.

questions.prompt: A mass \(m\) is tied to a fixed wall by a spring \(k\), with no damper. An external force \(u\) pushes the mass, and \(y\) is the stretch of the spring. Which equation is Newton's law?
questions.explanation: The spring force on the mass pulls back toward the unstretched position, so it enters with a minus: \(m\ddot y = u - ky\). A plus sign on \(ky\) would push the mass further out as it moves out, which is unstable. The mass multiplies acceleration, not velocity. Swapping \(m\) and \(k\) assigns inertia to the spring and a spring law to the mass.

questions.prompt: A rotor has inertia \(J = 0.4\ \mathrm{kg\,m^2}\) and viscous friction \(0.08\ \mathrm{N\,m\,s}\). A constant torque of \(0.16\ \mathrm{N\,m}\) is applied. What speed does it settle to, in rad/s?
questions.explanation:
\(J\dot\omega = \tau - b\omega\). In steady state \(b\omega = \tau\), so \(\omega = 0.16/0.08 = 2\ \mathrm{rad/s}\). The inertia cancels out of the resting speed. The time constant is \(J/b = 5\ \mathrm{s}\).
• \(0.16/0.4 = 0.4\) is the initial angular acceleration, in \(\mathrm{rad/s^2}\).
• \(0.4/0.08 = 5\) is the time constant, in seconds.
• \(0.16 imes 0.08\) is not a speed.

questions.prompt: A tank has surface area \(3\ \mathrm{m^2}\). Outflow is \(q = h/R\) with \(R = 0.4\ \mathrm{m/(m^3/s)}\). Inflow steps to \(0.5\ \mathrm{m^3/s}\). What height does the water settle to, in m?
questions.explanation:
Volume balance: \(3\dot h = 0.5 - h/0.4\). At rest, \(h/0.4 = 0.5\), so \(h = 0.2\ \mathrm{m}\). The area does not appear in the resting height. It appears in the time constant \(AR = 1.2\ \mathrm{s}\).
• \(0.5/3 = 0.167\) divides the inflow by the area. That is a velocity of the free surface only if nothing flows out.
• \(0.5 imes 3 = 1.5\) multiplies by the area.
• \(0.4\) is the resistance, not the height.

questions.prompt: A capacitor \(C = 200\ \mu\mathrm{F}\) charges from a \(10\ \mathrm{V}\) source through \(R = 5\ \mathrm{k\Omega}\). It starts at \(0\ \mathrm{V}\). What is the capacitor voltage at \(t = 1\ \mathrm{s}\), in V?
questions.explanation:
The element laws give \(C\dot v = (10 - v)/R\), or \(\dot v + v/(RC) = 10/(RC)\). Here \(RC = 5000 \times 200 \times 10^{-6} = 1\ \mathrm{s}\). The solution is \(v = 10(1 - e^{-t})\). At \(t = 1\), \(v = 10(1 - e^{-1}) = 6.32121\ \mathrm{V}\).
• \(10\) is the final voltage, reached only after several time constants.
• \(10/e = 3.679\) is the amount still missing, not the voltage reached.
• \(5\) would be a halfway guess. One time constant reaches about \(63\%\), not \(50\%\).

questions.prompt: Which pair can be the state of a circuit made of resistors, capacitors, and inductors?
options: The voltage across a resistor and the current through that same resistor
The source voltage and nothing else
The current through a resistor, because resistors store charge
questions.explanation: Inductors store energy in current, and capacitors store energy in voltage. Those are the quantities whose derivatives are fixed by the element laws, so they are the states. A resistor is algebraic: its voltage and current are locked by Ohm's law and do not need an initial condition. The source is an input, not a state. Calling a resistor a storage element double-counts a variable the algebra already removed.

questions.prompt: States of a mass-spring-damper are position and velocity, in that order. The parameters are \(m = 5\ \mathrm{kg}\), \(b = 4\ \mathrm{N\,s/m}\), \(k = 20\ \mathrm{N/m}\). In \(\dot x = Ax + Bu\), what is the entry in the second row and first column of \(A\)?
questions.explanation:
\(\dot x_1 = x_2\) and \(\dot x_2 = -(k/m) x_1 - (b/m) x_2 + u/m\). The \((2,1)\) entry is \(-k/m = -20/5 = -4\). The minus sign is the restoring spring. Writing the state equation this way is the step from a scalar ODE to a state-space model.
• \(+4\) drops the restoring sign.
• \(-20\) forgets to divide by the mass.
• \(-b/m = -0.8\) is the \((2,2)\) entry, the damping term.

questions.prompt: A vehicle of mass \(1200\ \mathrm{kg}\) has linear drag \(80\ \mathrm{N}\) per \((\mathrm{m/s})\). The engine holds a constant \(400\ \mathrm{N}\). There is no grade. What speed does it settle to, in m/s?
questions.explanation:
\(1200\,\dot v = 400 - 80 v\). At rest, \(v = 400/80 = 5\ \mathrm{m/s}\). This balance is the plant a cruise-control loop closes. The mass again sets the time constant \(1200/80 = 15\ \mathrm{s}\), not the cruising speed.
• \(400/1200 = 0.333\) is the initial acceleration in \(\mathrm{m/s^2}\).
• \(80/1200\) is the reciprocal time constant.
• \(400 imes 80\) is not a speed.

questions.prompt: A tank's time constant is \(8\ \mathrm{s}\). The behavior that matters lasts \(40\ \mathrm{s}\). How many time constants long is that window?
questions.explanation:
\(40/8 = 5\). Five time constants is long enough that a first-order transient has essentially settled, which is the kind of scaling check a modeling pass makes before adding more detail. Keeping the time constant and throwing away the horizon, or the reverse, answers a different question.
• \(8/40 = 0.2\) inverts the ratio.
• \(40 - 8 = 32\) subtracts instead of scaling.
